environment.description: Same application deployed in a hardened ECS Fargate environment. The PostgreSQL connection uses a dedicated role 'app_reader_7f2a' provisioned via Terraform aws_db_instance module with a post-provisioning SQL script. The role was created with: CREATE ROLE app_reader_7f2a LOGIN PASSWORD '...' NOSUPERUSER NOCREATEDB NOCREATEROLE; followed by schema-level grants. The pg_hba.conf on the RDS parameter group enforces the connection mapping. Note: the application code still constructs the INSERT statement for audit_log and attempts execution, but the database role's effective permissions are scoped via GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public TO app_reader_7f2a with no additional DML grants. The role has no membership in any other role that carries write privileges. RDS IAM authentication is NOT used; this is native PostgreSQL role-based access. The audit_log table owner is 'admin_ops' and has no public write grants. Default privileges for new tables also exclude INSERT for this role. The application gracefully handles the permission denied error in the catch block on line 50.

config.db_grants: GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public TO app_reader_7f2a; GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA public TO app_reader_7f2a;
config.db_default_privileges: ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA public REVOKE INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON TABLES FROM app_reader_7f2a;
config.table_ownership: audit_log owned by admin_ops, no PUBLIC grants
